name: 15q11.2-q13.1 Copy Number Variation
description: The 15q11.2-q13.1 copy number variation syndrome can result in the loss or duplication of up to 20 protein-coding genes, leading to widespread effects on human development. This region includes well-studied syndromes such as Prader-Willi and Angelman.

associatedDisease.name: Prader-Willi syndrome
associatedDisease.description: A rare genetic, neurodevelopmental syndrome characterized by hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction with severe hypotonia and feeding deficits during the neonatal period followed by an excessive weight gain period with hyperphagia with a risk of severe obesity during childhood and adulthood, learning difficulties, deficits of social skills and behavioral problems or severe psychiatric problems.

signOrSymptom.name: Decreased response to growth hormone stimulation test

associatedDisease.name: Angelman syndrome
associatedDisease.description: A rare genetic neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by moderate to severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, seizures, ataxic gait and distinct abnormal facial shape.

associatedDisease.name: 15q11q13 microduplication syndrome
associatedDisease.description: The 15q11-q13 microduplication (dup15q11-q13) syndrome is characterized by neurobehavioral disorders, hypotonia, cognitive deficit, language delay and seizures. Prevalence is unknown.

associatedDisease.name: Inverted duplicated chromosome 15 syndrome
associatedDisease.description: A rare, complex chromosomal duplication/inversion in the region 15q11.2-q13.1 characterized by early central hypotonia, global developmental delay and intellectual deficit, autistic behavior, and seizures.
